strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with interleaved scaling
strategies.desc: Performs 16 dependent all-reduce operations with scale/unscale operations between each, exactly as in the reference implementation. Total dispatch count is 16 all-reduces plus local element-wise ops that can fuse. Represents the baseline: maximum correctness, no structural optimization, highest latency due to sequential dependencies.

strategies.name: Batched all-reduce with fused local ops
strategies.desc: Groups multiple all-reduce rounds into batches where the scale/unscale pattern repeats, pre-computing scaling coefficients and fusing all local element-wise operations (clone, scale, divide) into single kernels between all-reduces. Reduces dispatch count by fusing ~48 local ops into ~16 fused kernels. Trades additional buffer management for fewer kernel launches.

strategies.name: Pipelined overlapping computation-communication
strategies.desc: Splits the 57344-element tensor into chunks and pipelines all-reduce operations on different chunks while computing scaling operations on already-communicated chunks. Uses async all-reduce launches where possible to overlap computation of scale/unscale with communication of next iteration. Requires 16× all-reduces but hides some local-op latency behind communication.

strategies.name: Hierarchical reduce-scatter and all-gather decomposition
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing per-rank sharding during intermediate computation phases. After reduce-scatter, each rank computes scaling only on its shard (1/W of data), then all-gather reconstructs full tensor. Reduces per-iteration computation volume by W-factor but doubles collective count to 32 operations.

strategies.name: Algebraic optimization with merged iterations
strategies.desc:
Observes that repeated scale→all-reduce→unscale patterns can be algebraically simplified by merging consecutive iterations where mathematical commutativity allows. Pre-computes compound scaling factors for groups of iterations, reducing the 16 dependent all-reduces to fewer operations (8-10) with adjusted coefficients. Minimizes both collective and local-op dispatch counts through mathematical transformation.
